speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) to date, how many companies have implemented portable medical benefits for their employees; (b) how can it be made more pervasive and attractive for both employers and employees to support such initiatives; and (c) apart from contributing to MediSave, whether portability of medical benefits can be in the form of reimbursements to employees for the premium that they pay for standard medical insurance.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the tripartite work group has been successful in encouraging employers and employees to shift to portable medical benefits; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider legislation to mandate that corporate outpatient medical insurance plans become portable in order to protect employees who may be unable to qualify for a subsequent insurance plan due to pre-existing conditions.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the company level, more than 90% of employers provide additional medical benefits.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Among them, some employers provide portable medical benefits on a voluntary basis.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: These companies may enjoy higher tax deductions for their medical expenses if they meet the qualifying conditions.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The tripartite partners are, therefore, promoting MediShield Life as the platform for voluntary portable benefits.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MediShield Life is universal and employees can use MediSave contributions to pay for premiums for MediShield Life, as well as Integrated Shield Plans which build on top of MediShield Life.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: More importantly, the annual claim limit has been raised significantly and the lifetime claim limit has been removed.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Our focus going forward is to encourage employers to shift from providing non-portable medical benefits, such as the Group Hospital and Surgical insurance, to making additional contributions to employees' MediSave accounts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The tripartite partners have, for a start, included this recommendation in the Tripartite Guidelines on the Re-employment of Older Employees released in May 2016.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will continue to encourage more employers to shift towards offering voluntary portable medical benefits which leverage on MediShield Life.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I just wish to clarify with a supplementary question.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Since the take-up rate is rather slow, about 4%, is there something more that we can do to entice employers to contribute more to MediSave?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The second point I would like to make is that benefits, besides being extended to the individual employee, employers do extend some benefits to their family members.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Thus, I wish to ask whether there can be some other incentives to allow employers to contribute to the immediate family members of the employee's family.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the part of the employers, many of them found it more effective for them to attract and retain the workers that they want; in other words, they can tailor their company's medical scheme as an attraction.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, employers adopt the shorter-term perspective.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It is more cost-effective for them to continue the current practice.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the part of the unions, they also find it a challenge to convince the workers to move towards portable medical benefits because, for most of the company-provided medical insurance schemes, the payment starts from the first dollar.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, there is no co-payment needed from the first dollar.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The challenge for the tripartite partners is to convince both the employers as well as the unions and workers to adopt a longer-term perspective.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Today, there are already financial incentives for employers to move towards portable medical benefits.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But I would say that the hurdles – in terms of how we overcome this short-term perspective of the workers and employers – would be something we will continue to work on through tripartite efforts.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Part of the question is whether employees have the opportunity to apply for portability.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many times, it is not a case of the employee not wanting to pay for the additional portability, but it is that they are not even given the opportunity by the employer.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: There are certain countries which mandate or legislate this portability, for example, the United States, through the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My second clarification is, especially with our economy going into a bit of a slowdown and we hear of retrenchments going on, aside from peace of mind that employees will get, sometimes also, because their family members have pre-existing conditions, for example, their wives or children may also be tagged to these corporate insurance schemes.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, it would help them very much if they can at least have the option of opting for this portability.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I would like the Minister to consider this point.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Basically, the schemes offered by the companies, or by the employers to the workers, would be through the Group Hospital and Surgical scheme.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For Page: 7 example, if a company were to offer their employees portability, there would be the option for the employee to either come under the group scheme or the individual scheme.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The healthier ones may go for the individual scheme.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MediShield Life is for everyone, including the family, children and spouses of the workers.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: The problem is MediShield Life only extends to inpatient insurance.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: What happens if the employee or the family members have huge, large like tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars in outpatient hospital bills?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If there are other areas of expensive and long-term outpatient treatment which the Member feels should be included in MediShield Life, he may wish to file a separate Parliamentary Question to the Health Minister.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: I just wish to again clarify with the Minister that in unionised companies, unions keep putting in effort to ensure that employers embrace portability through contributions to MediSave, but the concern is that there are many un-unionised companies.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: I also understand that there is a gap of understanding.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: MediShield Life has been very pervasive and people do understand what MediShield Life is.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: However, the part about portability, the contribution by employers to MediSave, it is that part that we need to create more awareness of.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: We need to ensure that people also know the advantage of having the money in MediSave, as it can earn interest, it is long term, it is portable and it grows.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Ms Thanaletchimi, can you put forward the question?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: So, I think we should do more and we need to have a concerted effort to educate and create awareness, both to the employees as well as employers.
